headline: The White House pulled its FDA pick. Not enough votes.
summary: The White House dropped Heidi Overton as its nominee to run the Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday night, the eve of her Senate committee vote. Republicans hold that committee by one vote. Its chair, Bill Cassidy, called her role in changing childhood vaccine advice 'almost disqualifying'. The FDA has had an acting head since May.

cover_question.q: Why can't he just pick someone?

cover_answer: He did pick. The Senate has to say yes, and it wouldn't.
table_question: If you picked a captain and the team said no, who decides?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president picked a new boss for the team that checks our food and medicine before stores can sell them. That boss needs the Senate to say yes first, the way a new teacher needs the principal's OK. Not enough senators would, so the president took the pick back. The team still checks everything. Nothing changes for you.
5-7.why: One job, checking medicine, and one rule: a yes comes first.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script hands over one job, checking medicine, and one rule, the grown-up needs a yes first. The principal's OK is a yes they have watched being given. Expect 'is my medicine still okay?' Yes. The checkers never stopped; only the boss's chair is empty.

8-12.script: Trump picked Heidi Overton to run the FDA in August. A Senate committee votes on picks like a hiring panel, and Republicans hold it by one seat, so one no from their side ends it. Chair Bill Cassidy called her vaccine work 'almost disqualifying'. The White House pulled her the night before the vote.
8-12.why: A one-vote margin is a chain they can count.
8-12.why_long: At nine a child is working out rules and whether adults apply them, so the script runs the chain: a pick in August, a panel one seat apart, one senator's doubt, a withdrawal the night before. The hiring panel is a mechanism they know from class votes. Expect 'so who's in charge of the FDA?' An acting boss, Kyle Diamantas, since May.

13-17.script: Should a doctor who helped change children's vaccine advice run the FDA? Republican Bill Cassidy called it 'almost disqualifying', and the White House pulled Heidi Overton before his committee voted. Second: Cassidy says the White House quit a winnable path. Who sets the bar?
13-17.why: Two readings: no votes, or a deal refused.
13-17.why_long: A sixteen-year-old can hold two true things: the White House says she lacked the votes, and Cassidy says it quit rather than make promises on abortion. The script gives them both accounts and asks who sets the bar. Expect 'does the president have to listen to the Senate?' For this job, yes. Without a vote there is no commissioner.

5-7.q: Why can't he just pick someone?
5-7.a: He did. But the Senate has to say yes first, and this time it wouldn't.

8-12.a: It checks medicines and food before they're sold. An acting boss runs it now.

8-12.q: Why did his own party say no?
8-12.a: Her work on kids' vaccine advice, the abortion pill and flavored vapes.

13-17.q: Should vaccine views decide who runs the FDA?
13-17.a: Cassidy thought so. Decide what you'd want in the job first.
Acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas, since May. Maybe for a while.
